intro.headline:

intro.body: Coach a fictional club through a season the engine truly simulates. Every instruction is legal hockey — and after full time the game shows you why it worked.
intro.support: No account. Works offline. 90 seconds to your first match.

onboarding.s1Title: Pick a club nobody has heard of
onboarding.s1: Two tiers of Belgian-flavoured clubs, twenty seasons of invented history. Every name, town and crest is generated — and checked so it belongs to no real club.
onboarding.s2Title: A season you can actually read
onboarding.s2: Play the match days or simulate them. Watch the table, the play-offs and the play-down; give youth minutes; keep the treatment room short.
onboarding.s3: Tactics, the penalty-corner battery, rotation on legs. Every instruction is legal hockey, and after full time the game shows you why it worked.

squad.title: Squad
squad.sub: {n} players · {youth} youth · wage bill {pct} % of a volunteer budget
squad.pick: Pick a player to read the coaching note.

read.gkReflex: A reflex keeper ({reflex}) more than a sweeper ({one}): keep the line deep and let the shots come to the pads.
read.gkOneOnOne: Strong one-on-one ({one}) — push the line up, the keeper closes the space behind it.
read.gkBalanced: A balanced keeper (reflexes {reflex}, one-on-one {one}). Shape the defence around the backs, not the keeper.
read.fwdBaseline: Quickest first three metres in the squad and comfortable receiving on the reverse — a baseline-entry forward, not a target man. Long-ball build-up wastes that: {goals} goals so far, the flank entry with a trailing runner is the pattern.
read.fwdFinisher: A finisher (hit {hit}): wants the ball on the spot strip, early. Build through the middle and get the ball to the top of the D.
read.fwdWorker: A worker (work rate {work}): the first presser, the runner who makes the second line press work. Worth more in a full-court press than in a low block.
read.midPlaymaker: Sees the pass (vision {vision}) — the outlet through the middle runs through this player. Protect the minutes in the last quarter.
read.midAerial: Comfortable in the air ({aerial}): the direct outlet over a press. On watered turf the flat ball is faster, so use it when pressed, not by default.
read.midEngine: An engine (work rate {work}, stamina {stamina}): rotates late, covers the press. Rotate below 55 % and this player plays all four quarters.
read.defFlicker: A drag flick of {flick} — the PC battery's striker. Protect the player from green cards: the battery without the flicker is a lost corner.
read.defStopper: A stopper (tackling {tackle}): the marker for their best runner in the D. Ask for the channel tackle, not the lunge.
read.defOutlet: An outlet defender (push {push}): plays the first pass from the 23. Width on the outlet, never the back pass into the D.

rules.title: The rulebook
rules.sub: FIH rules as the engine applies them — each one is data in packages/rules, not prose.

feet.title: Feet in the circle
feet.body: A ball that hits a defender's foot or body inside the circle is a penalty corner; outside the circle it is a free hit. The attacker who plays the ball at feet is within the rules — the defender must keep the body out of the line.

dangerous.title: Dangerous play
dangerous.body: A ball raised at an opponent within five metres above knee height is dangerous play: free hit against the striker, and a penalty corner or stroke if it happens in the circle.

backStick.title: Back-stick
backStick.body: Only the flat face of the stick may play the ball. The rounded side is a free hit.

obstruction.title: Obstruction
obstruction.body: Shielding the ball with the body, backing into an opponent or running across a player going for the ball is obstruction — a free hit.

stickTackle.title: Stick tackle
stickTackle.body: Hitting, hooking or holding an opponent's stick is a free hit; inside the circle a penalty corner.

freeHitDistance.title: Five metres at a free hit
freeHitDistance.body: Opponents must be five metres from the ball at a free hit. Standing closer — or rushing the restart — is a free hit to the other side.

selfPass23.title: Self-pass after a free hit inside the 23
selfPass23.body: The attacker may self-pass, but from a free hit inside the attacking 23 the ball must travel five metres or be touched by a defender before it enters the circle. Closing the five metres is how the defence kills it.

pcBreach.title: Breaking early at a penalty corner
pcBreach.body: Defenders behind the backline and attackers outside the circle must wait for the injection. A defender who breaks early is sent to the halfway line; an attacker who breaks early concedes a free hit.

pcFirstHit.title: The first hit at a penalty corner
pcFirstHit.body: The first shot at goal at a penalty corner, if it is a hit, must cross the goal line below 460 mm. A drag flick or a push may go at any height.

stroke.title: Penalty stroke
stroke.body: A stroke is awarded for an offence that prevents a probable goal or a deliberate foul in the circle. One push or flick from 6.4 m, the keeper on the line; the taker may not take it before the whistle.

circle.title: The circle rule
circle.body: A goal counts only if the ball was touched by an attacker inside the circle before crossing the goal line. Nothing scores from outside the D — which is why the whole game lives there.

pc.title: Penalty corner
pc.body: Injected from the backline ten metres from the post; five defenders plus the keeper behind the line, everybody else beyond the halfway line; the ball must leave the circle before a shot unless trapped at the top. Awarded for a foul by a defender in the circle or a deliberate one inside the 23.

cards.title: Cards
cards.body: Green: two minutes off. Yellow: five or ten minutes off. Red: the rest of the match. Persistent fouling escalates.

subs.title: Rolling substitutions
subs.body: Any number of substitutions at any time through the dugout gate — except during a penalty corner, when only the keeper may be replaced.

aerial.title: The aerial
aerial.body: A raised ball is legal when it is safe: not towards an opponent within five metres, and received by one player with opponents five metres away until it is controlled.

about.title: About BULLY OFF
about.intro: A field-hockey coach/manager game built on a deterministic match engine. Everything in it is fictional and everything runs on your device.
about.privacy1: No real clubs and no real people. Clubs, players, coaches and towns are generated from common-name pools and checked against a list of real clubs; no person is modelled, rated or named.
about.privacy2: No accounts, no telemetry, no analytics, no advertising. The app makes no network requests after it has loaded; your careers live in your browser's storage (IndexedDB) and in the files you export yourself.
about.privacy3: Replays and saves you export contain only generated data. Sharing them shares nothing about you.
about.privacy4: Club mode (entering your own squad) is not part of v1.0; when it comes it will be local-only and clearly marked.
about.offline: Installed as an app, BULLY OFF works without a connection: the engine, the world generator and your saves are local.
about.credits: Open source (MIT). Deterministic engine, FIH rules as data, a utility AI, a season model with twenty seasons of generated history, and a PixiJS replay viewer — calibrated against public Belgian League aggregates.
